topics.topic: Backup-look interval value and scheduling owner
questions: What exact interval does `BACKUP_LOOK_SECONDS` prescribe for the deterministic caller?
Which module imports and applies `BACKUP_LOOK_SECONDS` to schedule calls of `run_daily_backup_if_due`?

quotes:
Any limit or schedule: the 8 hours, 30, 15 and 10 minutes and the 60 seconds
are `data_provider`'s constants that `owner_sessions` applies, the 03:00 and
the minute look constants that `backups` applies.

The start and the running instance: `configuration` first, then the backup
probe and `store`, then the listeners at the release's addresses, serving
nothing until every check passed and having `store` remove a store this start
made new when a listener cannot be opened (A17 rule 2); the
owner-only start, which opens the owner interface alone (A17 rule 1, A18
rule 9); the two surfaces, the owner interface's listener opened first; the 60-second pass
of `owner_sessions` and the minute look of `backups` (A13 rule 2, A18 rule 1);
that a restart ends every owner session (A13 rule 2).
judgement.divergence: `backups` imports and applies the look-interval constant, or `instance_lifecycle` applies it while scheduling the minute look; `instance_lifecycle`, as the caller, notices which module owns the scheduling decision.
judgement.why: State 3 assigns application of the minute-look constant to `backups` but assigns ownership of the minute look and timers to `instance_lifecycle`.

topics.topic: Upload-stream receiver and pre-buffering size-limit enforcement
questions: Which module and capability receive the upload stream and enforce the declared-length and actual-byte limits before the owner interface or form parser buffers the file?

quotes:
`module:owner_interface` serves the upload, the mapping and the confirmation
pages.

`module:data_provider` holds the file's size limit
and the declared types as constants `module:migration_import` imports.

R0-29's server-rendered forms over the owner's operations. A19 rules 1 and 2:
every stored value rendered as text escaped for its place, no script of its
own, a content security policy forbidding any.

The import file is read as data with a size limit of 50 MB, 50 × 1024 ×
   1024 bytes (owner, 2026-11-11); nothing in it is executed or evaluated, and
   a file over the limit is refused before any of it is parsed. The limit is counted
   over the bytes Registry receives, never over a length the request
   declares: a declared length over the limit is refused before any byte is
   read; otherwise Registry reads the upload up to one byte more than the
   limit and refuses it as soon as it holds more than the limit, whatever
   length was declared or whether one was. A refused upload is kept nowhere
   and replaces no file the session kept (A16 rule 2). The limit is one
   value of the release, the data provider's constant
   `IMPORT_FILE_MAX_BYTES` = 52428800, which the code that receives the
   upload imports (SPEC_STANDARD §15.3.1); no other place holds it, and it
   is not configuration (A17 rule 1).
judgement.divergence: The owner-interface transport imports the limit and rejects an oversized declared length before reading or buffering a body, or it buffers file bytes and only `migration_import` applies the limit; the client and host operator notice whether upload bytes are requested and memory or network resources are consumed.
